{
  "hook": "Lake Neusiedl's heat retention pushes Blaufränkisch to full ripeness without losing acidity. This bottle leverages that microclimate to deliver dark fruit weight alongside the variety's signature iron grip. Consistent gold medals from the Berliner Wine Trophy confirm the estate's grip on this style across vintages.",
  "wine_summary": "Operating out of Oggau, the estate focuses on reducing yields to concentrate flavor without relying on oak heaviness. Unlike the schist-driven versions from Mittelburgenland, these wines show plumper fruit profiles due to the gravel and clay mix found near the water. You get varietal purity here rather than winemaking overlay, keeping the wine flexible for food pairing rather than locking it into a heavy stylistic box.",
  "terroir_expression": "Gravel and clay dominate the vineyard soils here, providing drainage while retaining enough water to stress the vines moderately. The proximity to the steppe lake creates high humidity, which demands careful canopy management to avoid rot, but ensures the grapes maintain acidity during hot summers. In the glass, this translates to a juicy core of dark cherry supported by a saline minerality rather than sharp rockiness.",
  "vinification_summary": "To preserve fruit integrity, fermentation occurs in stainless steel or large wooden casks. The winemakers utilize maceration, where grape skins stay in contact with the juice, to extract color and tannin without bitterness. Aging happens in used oak barrels to avoid vanilla overload, letting the peppery spice of the grape stand forward.",
  "food_pairing": "Viennese Tafelspitz with horseradish — the acidity cuts through the rich beef broth.\nMushroom risotto with porcini — earthy notes in the fungus match the iron tones in the wine.\nGrilled lamb chops with rosemary — tannins bind with the protein fat to soften the mouthfeel.\nNashville hot chicken — the fruit sweetness balances the spice heat.\nSmoked duck breast — the smoke complements the peppery finish.",
  "comparable_wines": "For similar acidity, try Moric Blaufränkisch — often more mineral-driven from limestone soils.\nUmathum Zweigelt offers same region presence with slightly softer tannins but comparable fruit weight.\nPriory Rochus Pinot Noir provides different grape variety but similar earthy structure and acid backbone.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with bright acidity and peppery dark fruit",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink now through 2024 to catch the primary fruit energy. Store horizontally at 55°F away from vibration to keep the cork sealed.",
  "value_assessment": "$20 to $25 places this directly against entry-level Bordeaux blends. Competitors like Heinrich Blaufränkisch often command a higher premium for similar quality. It is worth the cost because the acidity structure offers better food versatility than jammy New World alternatives at this price point.",
  "market_position": "You will find this wine on retail shelves as a bridge for customers moving away from Cabernet Sauvignon. Restaurant sommeliers place this on by-the-glass lists for guests seeking something beyond Pinot Noir. Collectors skip this label in favor of the estate's single-vineyard reserves.",
  "insider_take": "While the acidity offers versatility, it lacks the plush texture some expect from this price point. The tradeoff for freshness is a leaner mouthfeel that palates accustomed to California styles might find sharp. Buy it when you need a red that survives a meal rather than dominating it.",

parsed.hook: Lake Neusiedl's heat retention pushes Blaufränkisch to full ripeness without losing acidity. This bottle leverages that microclimate to deliver dark fruit weight alongside the variety's signature iron grip. Consistent gold medals from the Berliner Wine Trophy confirm the estate's grip on this style across vintages.
parsed.wine_summary: Operating out of Oggau, the estate focuses on reducing yields to concentrate flavor without relying on oak heaviness. Unlike the schist-driven versions from Mittelburgenland, these wines show plumper fruit profiles due to the gravel and clay mix found near the water. You get varietal purity here rather than winemaking overlay, keeping the wine flexible for food pairing rather than locking it into a heavy stylistic box.
parsed.terroir_expression: Gravel and clay dominate the vineyard soils here, providing drainage while retaining enough water to stress the vines moderately. The proximity to the steppe lake creates high humidity, which demands careful canopy management to avoid rot, but ensures the grapes maintain acidity during hot summers. In the glass, this translates to a juicy core of dark cherry supported by a saline minerality rather than sharp rockiness.
parsed.vinification_summary: To preserve fruit integrity, fermentation occurs in stainless steel or large wooden casks. The winemakers utilize maceration, where grape skins stay in contact with the juice, to extract color and tannin without bitterness. Aging happens in used oak barrels to avoid vanilla overload, letting the peppery spice of the grape stand forward.
parsed.food_pairing:
Viennese Tafelspitz with horseradish — the acidity cuts through the rich beef broth.
Mushroom risotto with porcini — earthy notes in the fungus match the iron tones in the wine.
Grilled lamb chops with rosemary — tannins bind with the protein fat to soften the mouthfeel.
Nashville hot chicken — the fruit sweetness balances the spice heat.
Smoked duck breast — the smoke complements the peppery finish.
parsed.comparable_wines:
For similar acidity, try Moric Blaufränkisch — often more mineral-driven from limestone soils.
Umathum Zweigelt offers same region presence with slightly softer tannins but comparable fruit weight.
Priory Rochus Pinot Noir provides different grape variety but similar earthy structure and acid backbone.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-bodied dry red with bright acidity and peppery dark fruit
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink now through 2024 to catch the primary fruit energy. Store horizontally at 55°F away from vibration to keep the cork sealed.
parsed.value_assessment: $20 to $25 places this directly against entry-level Bordeaux blends. Competitors like Heinrich Blaufränkisch often command a higher premium for similar quality. It is worth the cost because the acidity structure offers better food versatility than jammy New World alternatives at this price point.
parsed.market_position: You will find this wine on retail shelves as a bridge for customers moving away from Cabernet Sauvignon. Restaurant sommeliers place this on by-the-glass lists for guests seeking something beyond Pinot Noir. Collectors skip this label in favor of the estate's single-vineyard reserves.
parsed.insider_take: While the acidity offers versatility, it lacks the plush texture some expect from this price point. The tradeoff for freshness is a leaner mouthfeel that palates accustomed to California styles might find sharp. Buy it when you need a red that survives a meal rather than dominating it.
